name: Breakdown: See the Physics
subtitle: Pool trick shots, explained
promotional_text: New: Behind the 8-Ball. Twelve hooked spots on a full table. Call your ball, then kick, bank, jump or massé your way out and learn how to play it on a real table.
description:
Pool that shows its working.

Every shot in Breakdown comes with the physics behind it. Take the cue, hit the ball, then watch it happen in slow motion while the table explains itself.

NEW: BEHIND THE 8-BALL

Twelve real eight-ball situations where you are hooked behind other balls, each on a full table. Call your ball and pocket, or call Safety, then find a way out:

- Kick it off a cushion or bank it in
- Jump over the blocker or curve around it with massé and swerve
- Play a combination, or reach for the bridge

Every escape is scored: 5 points for making it as called, up to 5 more for difficulty and up to 5 for style. Earn bronze, silver and gold medals and watch your running total climb.

After each shot, an On a Real Table card tells you how to play it yourself: the aim in diamonds, the cue angle, the speed, where to strike the cue ball and the miss most people make. It sits right next to the solver's own numbers, along with the cloth's sliding friction, rolling resistance and cushion bounce.

A REAL CUE AND BRIDGE

A proper 3D cue lines up every shot and follows through. The mechanical bridge comes out when you need the reach, and both raise for jump and massé shots so you can see exactly how the stroke is played.

THE PHYSICS LENS

Switch it on and the shot slows down and explains each beat:

- Amber when a ball is sliding, cyan once it rolls, thicker when it is fast
- Momentum handed from one ball to the next
- Energy lost to the cloth and the cushions
- A plain-words card for every collision, with the numbers behind it

Scrub through any shot, pause it, rewind your miss, change the spin or the aim and see exactly what was different. Ride along with the cue ball if you want the view from the cloth.

SURFACES AND TABLES

Play on tournament cloth with fast, lively cushions, or on worn dive-bar felt. Then try ice, glass, rubber, cork, carpet, sand and the Moon. Your surface applies to trick shots too, so you can see how the same shot changes.

Three new tables to play around on:

- Bumper pool, with posts and a cup at each end
- Five-pin billiards, with no pockets and five pins in the middle
- Bar billiards, with holes in the bed and skittles that must stay standing

ALSO IN THE GAME

- Ten trick shots: Watch it first, then Your turn
- Free play on any table and surface
- Real spin and aim: drag on the table, pull back for power, and touch the cue ball for follow, draw or side
- Title music to set the mood
- Built for everyone: screen reader support, larger text and fine sliders for the precise shot

Pool, but nerdier. We mean that as a compliment.

Breakdown runs on an exact physics solver, so the same shot always gives the same result. Nothing is faked and nothing is random unless you change it.
